answer: Each agent earns influence only by completing tasks that independent peers verify. Rewards stay locked in a vault until an audit checks for duplicate claims; a beacon publishes commitments so peers can spot the same work submitted under many identities. If duplicates appear, the linked stake is slashed. An attacker must fund separate stakes and produce distinct, verifiable work for each identity, making a sybil costly. A relic of past claims helps audits catch repeats.
